[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering HTTP Caching in REST APIs: ETags, Cache-Control, and Conditional Requests"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"HTTP caching is one of the most effective ways to scale REST APIs, reduce network latency, and minimize server load. By leveraging browser and intermediary proxy caches properly, clients can avoid downloading data that has not changed."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Role of Cache-Control"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Cache-Control header is the primary mechanism for defining caching policies in HTTP/1.1. It uses directives to control who can cache a response and for how long."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"no-cache: Forces caches to submit the request to the origin server for validation before releasing a cached copy."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"no-store: Prevents any caching of the response. Use this for highly sensitive data like banking details."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"public: Indicates that the response may be cached by any cache, including public CDNs."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"private: Indicates that the response is intended for a single user and should not be cached by shared proxies."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"max-age=<seconds>: Specifies the maximum amount of time a resource is considered fresh."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Conditional Requests and Validation"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once a cached resource expires, the client does not necessarily need to download it again. Instead, it can perform a conditional request. If the server verifies the resource has not changed, it replies with a lightweight 304 Not Modified status, omitting the response body."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding ETags"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"An ETag (Entity Tag) is an opaque identifier assigned by a web server to a specific version of a resource found at a URL. It is often a cryptographic hash (like MD5 or SHA-256) of the resource representation."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600
ETag: "33a64df551425fcc55e4d42a148796d9f" 

{"id": 1, "name": "Product A"}"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Conditional Requests in Clients"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"When making a subsequent request for an expired resource, the client sends the ETag value back to the server using the If-None-Match header."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"GET /api/products/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
If-None-Match: "33a64df551425fcc55e4d42a148796d9f""},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Handling Conditional Requests on the Server"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"The server intercepts the incoming If-None-Match header, compares it with the current ETag of the requested resource, and responds accordingly."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600
ETag: "33a64df551425fcc55e4d42a148796d9f""},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for REST API Caching"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always combine Cache-Control with validation mechanisms like ETags or Last-Modified headers."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use strong ETags for precise byte-for-byte comparisons, and weak ETags (prefixed with W/) when semantic equivalence is sufficient."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid caching state-changing methods like POST, PUT, and DELETE unless explicitly invalidated."}]
